stories.title: Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin–CD9 axis links severe neonatal intestinal injury to brain inflammation
stories.takeaway: A Nature study identifies Delta toxin from a subset of C. perfringens strains as a candidate driver of necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) and systemic injury through the host receptor CD9.
stories.what_happened: Published October 28, the authors combined clinical NEC samples, a genome-wide CRISPR screen, intestinal organoids, cell-specific Cd9-knockout mice and a neutralizing antibody. They report preferential macrophage targeting, inflammasome activation, blood–brain barrier disruption and protection by anti-Delta toxin in neonatal mouse infection models.
stories.why_it_matters: Provides a publicly documented example of connecting a microbial virulence factor to host-cell specificity and systemic inflammatory consequences, relevant to intestinal disease mechanisms and translational host–microbe modeling.
stories.caveat: The proposed mechanism concerns a subset of NEC, not all cases. Antibody protection is preclinical; larger clinical cohorts and an isogenic toxin-deletion strain are still needed.

stories.title: Caco-2 spheroids and an intestinal chip reveal nanoplastic-associated epithelial stress
stories.takeaway: A combined 3D spheroid and microfluidic intestinal model detected oxidative, inflammatory and epithelial changes after exposure to 20-nm polystyrene nanoplastics.
stories.what_happened: In an October 28 npj Science of Food article, researchers exposed Caco-2-derived cultures to polystyrene nanoparticles, measuring antioxidant capacity, inflammatory markers, Villin and ZO-1, and chip-effluent metabolites. Changes were reported at 40 and 400 micrograms per millilitre; computational analyses nominated ALOX5 as an exploratory candidate.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows how engineered epithelial culture systems can integrate structural, functional and metabolic endpoints in exposure assessment and food-safety research.
stories.caveat: The tested concentrations should not be assumed to reflect typical human exposure; ALOX5 involvement was computationally suggested, not causally established by the reported assays.

stories.title: Patient-derived renal cancer assembloids reconstruct tumour–fibroblast–T-cell interactions
stories.takeaway: Mix-and-match tumour assembloids identify a WNT–activin A axis linking cancer-associated fibroblasts to CD8 T-cell state and response to PD-1 blockade.
stories.what_happened: Published October 28 in Nature, the study recombined renal tumour cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts and immune cells from patient samples. Six patient-derived assembloid models were compared with parental tumours and therapeutic responses, with engineered assembloids and humanized mice used to investigate WNT-responsive fibroblasts and activin A signaling.
stories.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the experimental value of reconstituting multiple human tissue compartments rather than studying epithelial or tumour cells in isolation.
stories.caveat: The initial patient-matched cohort was small, and predictive performance for routine treatment selection needs larger prospective validation.

stories.title: Compact Cas12m system enables multiplex CRISPR gene activation from one AAV vector
stories.takeaway: An engineered naturally nuclease-dead Cas12m variant processes guide arrays and supports coordinated activation of endogenous genes within an all-in-one viral delivery design.
stories.what_happened: A Nature Biotechnology paper published October 28 describes denCas12m and the smCRISPRa platform. The system processes multiple guide RNAs from a single transcript and demonstrated phenotypic rescue in mouse models of Duchenne muscular dystrophy and Scn1a haploinsufficiency.
stories.why_it_matters: Expands the engineering toolbox for combinatorial gene regulation and may inform future programmable cell and gene therapies.
stories.caveat: The reported therapeutic demonstrations are in mice; delivery efficiency, off-target activity and durable safety require further evaluation in human settings.

stories.title: Droplet long-read single-cell epigenomics scales chromatin profiling to thousands of cells
stories.takeaway: dscNanoATAC and dscNanoCUT combine droplet microfluidics with Nanopore sequencing to resolve allele-specific chromatin accessibility and histone modifications.
stories.what_happened: A Cell Discovery article published October 27 reports throughput of roughly 5,000 cells per experiment, profiling cultured mammalian cells and mouse brain. Long reads enabled analyses of regulatory elements in difficult-to-map regions, allele-specific Ube3a regulation and computational prediction of haplotype-resolved chromatin structure.
stories.why_it_matters: Offers a high-throughput approach to examining regulatory heterogeneity across cell populations and complements transcriptome-focused single-cell studies.
stories.caveat: The methods do not simultaneously capture gene expression, and long-read fragment yield and some cell-recovery metrics remain limiting.
